paper_title: Let the Expert Stick to His Last Expert-Specialized Fine-Tuning for   Sparse Architectural Large Language Models
caption: Results of the shared Top-6 routed experts in two independent samples of a task. The x-axis represents the sample size, and the y-axis shows the shared Top-6 routed experts averaged by model layers.
model_annotation: This plot illustrates the number of shared experts across two independent samples of a task, as a function of sample token count. The x-axis is labeled "Sample Token Count" and uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10<sup>9</sup> to 10<sup>20</sup>, with tick labels at 10<sup>9</sup>, 10<sup>10</sup>, 10<sup>11</sup>, 10<sup>12</sup>, 10<sup>13</sup>, 10<sup>14</sup>, 10<sup>15</sup>, 10<sup>16</sup>, 10<sup>17</sup>, and 10<sup>18</sup>. The y-axis is labeled “Shared Experts for Two Samples” and uses a linear scale ranging from 3.8 to 6.0, with tick marks at 3.8, 4, 4.5, 5, 5.5, and 6.0. A red solid line, without markers, begins at 4.1 at 10<sup>9</sup> and increases to 5.8 at 10<sup>18</sup>. A blue solid line, without markers, starts at 4.2 at 10<sup>9</sup> and declines to 2.8 at 10<sup>11</sup>, after which it steadily increases to 5.4 at 10<sup>18</sup>. A green solid line, without markers, begins at 4.4 at 10<sup>9</sup> and increases steadily to 5.5 at 10<sup>18</sup>. A gray solid line, without markers, begins at 4.3 at 10<sup>9</sup> and increases gradually to 5.2 at 10<sup>18</sup>. A purple solid line, without markers, begins at 4.0 at 10<sup>9</sup> and increases to 5.7 at 10<sup>18</sup>. A teal solid line, without markers, begins at 4.1 at 10<sup>9</sup> and increases to 5.6 at 10<sup>18</sup>.
